subject: library-science
intro: Library and information science leads to the people who organise knowledge itself — curating collections, building the systems that retrieve it, and guarding the public's access to it.

roles.title: Librarians and Media Collections Specialists
roles.what: Administer libraries and other information collections for public or private access — acquiring and cataloguing materials, managing databases and media, and running user services that locate information and teach people how to find it, in schools, universities, museums and corporations.
roles.where: Unit 2's cataloguing, classification and metadata schemas are the daily work of collection specialists; unit 3's Boolean and ranked retrieval underpins search and database support; units 4 and 5 cover the reference interview and collection development.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Appraise, edit and direct the safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents, then make them usable — describing collections, preserving fragile materials and supporting research built on the archives in their care.
roles.where: Unit 6 is the direct match: archival appraisal and description, preservation and conservation, and digital preservation. Unit 2's metadata schemas and unit 8's ethics of access shape how archives are described and opened to users.

roles.title: Museum Technicians and Conservators
roles.what: Prepare and care for museum collections: install exhibits, catalogue objects, and carry out the conservation and preservation work that keeps artefacts and records stable and accessible to researchers and visitors.
roles.where: Cataloguing and metadata from unit 2 and the preservation and digital-preservation topics of unit 6 apply directly to collection care; unit 5's licensing and digital collections cover managing materials people view on site or online.

roles.title: Library Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach library and information science at colleges and universities — courses in cataloguing, reference services, collection management and information ethics — often combining classroom teaching with research on how information is organised and used.
roles.where: The whole ALA-aligned curriculum is the syllabus they deliver: information organisation and retrieval, reference and user services, collections, archives, management, and the ethics of access and technology from units 1 to 8.
